utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can we have P22 -- sorry, 2723.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, there's an explanation, because you didn't want to learn the whole of it. You asked whether this was assistance to the VRS, but as a matter of fact, things were a bit different than that. The assets mentioned here were modified by the VJ in 1994, and those modified assets, when tested, presented certain problems with regard to reliability, use. The asset in question is called Koseva [phoen], which was introduced in operative use with all the problems that existed. Towards the end of 1994, a similar asset was used by the VRS. I presume that an arrangement had been reached to try and test it in operational use so as to deal with the problems our system had. I know that we modified our weapons system following that, removing a few flaws that had existed, and I believe that can be illustrated by some documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Djokic, let me remind you something. You may have heard me earlier asking Mr. Thomas how long he is going to be with you. It's Friday, I'm sure you'd like to go back home; and if you give short answers to questions and try to listen carefully to what is being asked, you are likely to go home quicker. With these kind of long answers, you are likely going to be here next week. So ...

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Can we have -- thank you, Your Honour. Could we have 2723 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir, this is another request from the VRS, signed by General Mladic, addressed to General Perisic personally. It is a request for -- I'm sorry, I'm looking at the wrong document. No, it's a request for six nitrogen tanks for use with surface-to-air rockets. Now, that's something that would have come within the technical department of the air force and air defence; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Does that explain, sir, why, at the top of the document in General Perisic's handwriting, he has written, "check also with Djokic"?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "Vucinic," who was my boss, and then, "check with Djokic" because this was within my remit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can we please have P2746 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: This is another request -- I'm sorry, sir, this is another request, yes, from General Mladic, again addressed to the Chief of the General Staff; this time for air-bombs. And at the very bottom of the document -- oh, no, before I ask you that. Again, that -- the supply of air-bombs would have been something that came within the purview of the technical administration of the air force and air defence sector; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not correct. It was within the competence of the aeronautical administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So let's go to the bottom of the document in English and also in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If that is so, sir, can you explain to me why the chief of cabinet, who presumably knows these things, has addressed the air force and air defence sector, saying that the Chief of the General Staff has approved that the VRS for this to be resolved as soon as possible in asking for the response of the air force and anti-aircraft defence sector?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was standard procedure because the RV and PVO sector is subordinated to the Chief of Staff. The RV and PVO sector has its various administration, such as air force administration, anti-aircraft units administration, et cetera. The RV and PVO sector was superior to those administrations and I worked in one such administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, what is your relationship with General Miletic who stood trial here as part of those accused of Srebrenica crimes?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Miletic is a friend of mine whom I had met when I worked in the aeronautical technical institute.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And do you remain firm friends, sir?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so. I asked for an approval to visit him.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General Miletic, you will know, was sentenced to 19 years' imprisonment for his part in the crimes at Srebrenica. And for his defence did you provide a statement describing him or referring to his honesty, profound morality, and integrity?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what I know about him from being close to him privately.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, sir, how do you reconcile that with the fact that he is a convicted war criminal?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I do believe the matter is not yet resolved and the case is on appeal. And I also don't think the question as put is proper. Two individuals being friends, irrespective of the errors of one, does not necessarily mean they still cannot be held with certain regard. If that was not the case, then the human race would probably not have much do with each other at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: That was a nice speech, sir, and I can rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Does Mr. Miletic's conviction for his part in the crimes at Srebrenica change your view of his profound morality?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How have you changed it, Mr. Thomas? Mr. Guy-Smith -- part of Mr. Guy-Smith's objection is that the matter is still under appeal; it's not finalised. But you're still going back to the conviction, which is still under appeal.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, I accept it's still under appeal, but, of course, he's been convicted. So at the moment that is his status.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's a curious reading of impeachment. If one is -- if this is being used for impeachment, which it clearly is, then the issue still remains that with regard to what the ultimate outcome will be of Mr. Miletic's conviction, it is an open question. If it was a final conviction, then there would be a different argument. But it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I can ask a different question.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir, do you still hold the view that General Miletic is a man of profound morality?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Do you accept that thousands of Bosnian Muslims were executed at Srebrenica and forcibly transferred by the VRS?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand that. But I also understand that General Miletic's wife --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... pause, sir.

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- is Muslim, and I associate with her frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Pause, sir. I'm not asking you about General Miletic. I'm just asking you if you accept that several thousand Bosnian Muslims were executed and forcibly transferred by the VRS at Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He has answered that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: He said he understands that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Does he accept that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I accept that there were crimes committed during the conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina that were committed. That is my understanding of the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Is that the extent of your acceptance, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me. The manner in which the question is asked, it seems as if Mr. Thomas has become a priest and he's asking for a confession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure what to make of that statement, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, when he says "is that the extent of your acceptance," the witness has said: "I accept that there were crimes committed during the conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina that were committed. That is the [sic] understanding of my [sic] problem." That's a relatively expansive answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you say he's asking like a priest seeking a confession --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is that the extent of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- and you stop there, I'm not quite sure what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I was referring to the statement, "is that the extent of your acceptance." His statement is all in -- is indeed all inclusive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks for the comment. Yes, Mr. Thomas, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So, sir, your answer that you accept that there were crimes committed during the conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina, is that the extent to which you are prepared to acknowledge the crimes at Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What other extent do you want from the witness, Mr. Thomas?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir, I asked him if he accept -- very specifically, if he accepted that several thousand Bosnian Muslim men were executed and forcibly transferred by the VRS. He would not accept that. All he would say is that there were crimes committed in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And we are all clear on the difference between you and the witness. Now, are you able to answer the question, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the question itself I was asked whether I was aware that several thousand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'm going to stop -- I'm going to stop you. I'm stopping you right there. You were asked if you accept that several thousand Muslims were murdered in Srebrenica. You said you understand that. The question is -- you understand that crimes were committed. Now, the question -- the next question is: Do you -- is that the extent of your acceptance, that only crimes were committed; and are you not prepared to accept that several thousand Muslims were killed? Now, sir, your answer is going to be: Yes, I do accept; no, I don't accept. Don't elaborate. Please. We want to finish quickly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do accept.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir, we've' heard evidence in this trial about modified air-bombs. How air-bombs were designed to be dropped from the air but they were modified to be able to be launch -- be launched from the ground. And we've heard about their use and the consequences of their use. You were the architect of that modification, were you not?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true. I was a member of the team, and I was in charge of a single segment. There was a whole team that worked on modifications.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, General Perisic considered you to be the architect of that modification, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if he did, then he was wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, let's have a look at that. Do you accept, sir, that you travelled in December 1994 to Bosnia to supervise the launching of air-bombs by the VRS?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there, but not to oversee the launching. I had not been trained for that, and it does not fall within anything I have ever done.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, what was your role?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am an air force technical engineer. I have a technical background. I cannot oversee any launching. I can only control the technical aspects of an asset. The role we had at the time - I don't know whether it was December, but in any case in late 1994 - was to pin-point the operational problems of those assets so as to be able to deal with similar problems that we had with our own assets of that kind. There is documentation in existence to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, your role -- well, what was your role, sir, in the design of this modified air-bomb, or in the concept?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The role the sector headed by me was in the institute to design the electronic part of the system designed to ignite the engines.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir, when were you promoted to chief of the air force technical administration?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: What was your next promotion, sir?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next promotion was in 2000. I was appointed chief of the operational logistics administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Did you have any change in rank, sir, between 1994 and 2000?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was promoted to the rank of general in 1997. However, it was one year later than would otherwise have been, had the standard time durations been observed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. So I want to talk about that 1997 promotion and the path taken to it. Are you aware -- well, your promotion would have been discussed at the VJ collegium, collegium of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You are aware, on the 28th of October, 1995, that General Perisic said the following of you: "I know him personally. He is a very intuitive man who successfully designed and modified an aircraft bomb to fit the launcher. He is an exceptional personality but alas he never got a doctor's degree. Once he gets that, we can decree him as well." I have a number of questions. First of all, sir, did you get your doctorate?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I received my Ph.D. in 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And then you were appointed to -- promoted to general?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not. Following the proposal of General Ljubisa Velickovic, I remained in the same rank for another year, although I had the right to be promoted immediately following my Ph.D.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: No, we understand that, sir. But subsequent upon getting your Ph.D. you were promoted to general?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, "He is a very intuitive man who successfully designed and modified an aircraft bomb to fit the launcher." Does that describe what you did?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does, and it's consistent with my previous answer that we modified the electric -- the electronic system for the ignition of the engine in my sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Once you had, or your department, come up with this concept and after you had made the necessary modifications, did you monitor how these modified air-bombs were being used and their effect?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the moment when the technical service hands over an asset, it no longer supervises it. It is done by the artillery administration. Following the development of the -- of an asset in charge of its further supervision is the artillery administration. And if it feels that it is required, they can contact us for any further remedial action if that is what -- if that is necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: General Djokic, you are an engineer. You invent a modification for a weapon. It is sent to the VRS. It is being deployed in combat. Are you telling us that notwithstanding your obvious professional interest in knowing how it was being used, notwithstanding that, you never found out how it was being used or its effects?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas, the ordnance which we modified was not sent to Republika Srpska. After our development, that asset was handed over to the artillery administration of the VJ and has been in use in the Yugoslav Army to this day. I don't know what dispatching are you talking about. It was not sent anywhere. It is within the VJ artillery administration as one of its standard assets.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, you would have been aware, sir, that modified air-bombs were being used by the VRS?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you have any knowledge at the time in what capacity and what effect they were having?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards to the actual effect of those bomb, I'm quite aware of their potential effect on the basis of technical data and on the bases of my own knowledge of this asset. It is primarily designed to target fortified objectives, pill boxes, bunkers, bridges, and what have you. Such a designed asset has the characteristics required to target such targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir, that on the 26th of November, 1997, again in discussion regarding you and your promotion, General Perisic said this: "In that sense, he is also an innovator, because something that could not have been used in this auditorium, he made it in such a way that it is being used from the ground. And everything went topsy-turvy whenever it was used, but that's just among us." Firstly, were you aware of General Perisic holding that view?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I hear of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Did you yourself ever express concerns to General Perisic about the problems that might be associated with using modified air-bombs?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I reported to the responsible administration which is the artillery administration about all problems, and I did so in writing. And it was their duty to caution General Perisic about any potential problems. This was standard procedure, and that's what I followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, you've talked about the sorts of targets that it's designed to attack. Is it a feature of modified air-bombs that they cannot be guided and that they are essentially inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that this asset does not have the facility for guiding. But as regards precision, precision from the air and from the ground is more or less the same. The median error in the worst of conditions can be about 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, is it an appropriate weapon to use in urban areas where there are civilian -- Sarajevo for example?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That asset was not at all planned nor designed to be used in urban communities.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Were you aware that it was being used in urban communities?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know derives from the reports that I read now which were made about their use, and I am aware that they were used in this way, which I considered to be totally inappropriate and wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And did you voice those concerns at the time, sir?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I had no information. I didn't have this data that you're now referring to. But to go back to this, in order for anyone to caution anybody else about the use of any assets that someone had to be in charge of it. And for the use of this asset, the only one in charge was the artillery administration. So it was the chief of the artillery administration whose asset it was that had to caution the Chief of the General Staff about the use of that asset which he introduced as part of the weaponry arsenal and of its potential effects.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. That concludes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thomas. Mr. -- any re-examination, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, could we please have P2746 up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before you start, Mr. Guy-Smith, let me ask you the same question I asked Mr. Thomas: How long are you likely to be with this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I do not expect that I will be with the witness for more than a half an hour, which exceeds the time of the day, which I know -- I made some requests with both the usher and I spoke to your Legal Officer about whether or not there would be a potential for us to have an extended session today. I don't know whether or not the Chamber has received that information or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, but the Chamber only works on what it gets as a formal request. There was an indication that the parties might make that request.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I could have jumped up and -- I didn't make the request. I'm making the request. I don't know whether or not it's feasible or not. If it's not feasible, this is my problem: My problem is I'm scheduled to leave the jurisdiction to go attend to other matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, the problem is that making the request at this point in time, certain arrangements have to be made. And I don't know whether they will be made -- they can be made between now and quarter to 2.00 and whether there is -- that staff is available to do that, you know. There are a lot of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm confident there's been some inquiry in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I am told that we might be able to sit until half past 3.00, assuming that everybody is available and agreeable to sitting. So you may go ahead, and we'll probably sit until half past 3.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, we may have to sit 15 bis. That also depends on the availability of everybody else. I haven't, sort of, inquired. I'm not sure whether everybody else is available. From the interpreters, is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. I'm advised that everybody has been consulted. So we will sit until 3:30. Before you carry on again Mr. Guy-Smith, I'm sorry to do this. Mr. Thomas, apparently you quoted from pages 79 and 81, quoting Mr. Perisic. Can you please give sources of number and documents, if possible, so that we know exactly what it is you were quoting.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, I can, sir. I don't have those with me immediately, but I'll provide those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Would you like me to proceed for the next five minutes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you would, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we please have P2746 up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you please tell us the date of this document.

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 7th of October, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to the request for modified air-bombs, what is the request focused at? And by that I'm referring to the language in the first two lines of the paragraph starting: "In order ..."

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not an expert on tactical use, but what is stated here is that this asset is being requested in order to regain lost features in the zone of responsibility or lost facilities in the zone of responsibility of the Herzegovina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to the term "facilities," could you explain to us in a military sense what lost facilities would entail?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the military sense, it means that you have lost a military position that you had held, that the enemy has taken up positions in that area, has taken over the area, and that now you wanted to regain the area which you used to hold by some more efficient means.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There has been some discussion with regard to the accuracy or inaccuracy of air-bombs in general. First of all, what I'd like to understand is, I believe on page 80 you indicated that air-bombs are a standard asset of the VJ army to this day. And that's at page 80, line 17 through 20. In order for a weapon to become a standard asset, what testing is required?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For an asset to become an official asset in using the VJ there are two kind of tests that it has to be subjected to. The first are development tests which are conducted by the institute in charge of the assets' development. And there are so-called admission tests, when all the requirements set before that particular asset have to be satisfied. Following this, a second test: The asset is then received, admitted into the weaponry of the army via an order, and its use starts thence forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the -- these assets as they relate to the VJ army, do you know whether or not the procedure that you have just described was performed?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. There's not a single weapon, a single asset, in the VJ that had not been subjected to the regular procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to those assets that were independently held by the VRS, do you know what testing procedures they went through, if any?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can talk about that only on the basis of the documents which I had occasion to study while working on this expert report, and pursuant to those documents I can say that they neither conducted any tests nor follow the procedure for the proper commissioning of those weapons for use in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I note the time. I assume that this is the appropriate time to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Guy-Smith, that is indeed. We'll take a break and come back at half past 2.00. Court adjourned. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.47 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we continue, may the record show that we are now sitting pursuant to 15 bis -- Rule 15 bis this afternoon. Judge Picard not being able to be with us due to prior engagements. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we please have P746 up on the screen. And I believe it's the initial pages of that document in both B/C/S and in English. I'm sorry, that -- we should be in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You've had some discussion with Mr. Thomas concerning this particular session, and I would just like to start at the very beginning. And if you could identify for us the individuals who were involved in the session the Supreme Defence Council held on the 7th of February, 1994?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the minutes, the session was attended by Zoran Lilic, the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia; Slobodan Milosevic, the president of the Republic of Serbia; Momir Bulatovic, the president of the Republic of Montenegro; Rade Kontic, the federal prime minister; Nikola Sainovic, the prime minister of the Republic of Serbia; Milo Djukanovic, the prime minister of the Republic of Montenegro; Pavle Bulatovic, the federal defence minister; Lieutenant-General Momcilo Perisic, chief of the General Staff; and Major-General Slavko Krivosija, chief of the military office of the FRY president.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As you have discussed, you've had occasion to review numerous sessions of the SDC. And with regard to the presence of Mr. Lilic, the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia; Mr. Kontic, the federal prime minister; and Mr. Bulatovic, the federal defence minister; could you tell the Chamber, please, based on your review, whether or not those individuals were present at -- regularly present at sessions of the Supreme Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Having perused the minutes of the sessions, I can say that the SDC members regularly attended, namely the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, the president of the Republic of Serbia, and the president of the Republic of Montenegro. In addition to them, the defence minister and the Chief of the General Staff also attended. And this would be the regular attendees of the sessions of the SDC.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please go to, I believe it's page 53 in the English and page 40 in the B/C/S of this particular session. Oh, I'm sorry, this is the -- I do apologise, these are the minutes. While we're here then -- see, this is what happens when you move too fast. Could we go to page 3 in the B/C/S and page 3 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I'd like to focus your attention, if I could, on section 2.4 and specifically number 2.4, para 2. And with regard to the conversation that you were having with Mr. Thomas earlier concerning Perisic's concerns about the federal Law on Property, is this the decision that was made at the conclusion of the discussion as reflected in the minutes of the Supreme Defence Council, that being that: "Pursuant to the federal Law on Property, a decision to give federal funds and aid to Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina shall be passed by the federal government, which shall place funds at the disposal of the Yugoslav Army General Staff for further operational work;"?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The council concluded here that action was to be taken pursuant to the law, which means that the federal government decided on property, and the General Staff was to implement its decisions operationally.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I thank you. That can be taken off the screen --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Just beforehand, Your Honour, it's taking it out of context simply to put inclusion number 2, sir, when there is conclusion number 5 as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Not with regard to the conversation that Mr. Thomas was having with him. And if he wishes to deal with that, he can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I don't see how -- okay, anyway. The Chamber does note conclusion number 5, and I don't know how that affects conclusion number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: This exhibit can be taken off. And could we please now have, I believe it's P752 which should be the stenographic notes of the 18th Session. I'm sorry, it's 792. Stop. 782, yes. I was correct. 788. P782. Now I'm going to refer to, if I could, page 40 in the B/C/S and I believe it's page 53 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to this particular session -- it is has not yet come up in B/C/S. There we go. Although it's ... Mr. Thomas, in his examination with you, was kind enough to read you what Mr. Perisic said in the context of the issue of the law; however, his conversation was somewhat short. And I'd like to continue with what was said by Mr. Kontic. First of all, if we could identify once again just for purposes of clarity, who was Mr. Kontic?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Kontic was the federal prime minister. And he was, so to speak, the boss of the -- to the minister of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to Mr. Kontic's response to Perisic's concerns and question, Mr. Kontic says, and I quote: "With the entry into force of the new Law on Federation Property, the federal government is the owner of the property as a whole. It's the federal government's to dispose of. It takes over everything. We will establish a staff, a ministry, an agency, which will be -- managed that vast property. We want to derive revenue from that property. We have to resolve a lot of questions with the Yugoslav Army concerning" -- could I see the next page, please, in English; it remains the same in B/C/S. "... this. One of these questions is the following: We have to resolve this question in conformity with the law. The Supreme Council cannot authorise someone to do that; only the government can do it. I suggest that within the framework of what we've agreed that belongs to us on the basis of the budget, we should decide at whose disposal we should place this - either at that of the Chief of the General Staff or the General Staff so he can work on it operationally." And then it says that Mr. Lilic comes in. And for purposes, again, of the record, could you please tell us who Mr. Lilic was at the time?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lilic was the president of the Supreme Defence Council in his capacity of president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: His comment is ... if you would be so kind as to tell us what he said?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "All right, we agree."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That document can be taken off the screen at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, with regard to issues concerning who had --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We can go back into open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to issues concerning who had control and authority - now I'm dealing with issues one might suggest chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we please have P1009 on the screen, which is the document that you spoke to Mr. Thomas about.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And while the document is coming up on the screen, apart from being the president, as defined, was Mr. Lilic or was he not the supreme commander?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards that question, there was always a discussion, a controversy, but in essence he is the supreme commander who orders -- who makes decisions and issues orders on the basis of the decisions taken by the Supreme Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the relationship between Lilic and Perisic, how would you characterise that relationship with regard to who can order who?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lilic could issue orders to Perisic with respect to the affairs that fall under the jurisdiction of General Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we have the next page in B/C/S, please. Third page in B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, with regard to what you've just told us, can the government order Perisic to engage in a particular act?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lilic, as the president of the Supreme Defence Council, could order Perisic only concerning the work and tasks which fall under the competency of the General Staff. Nothing outside of that. This is something that was defined by law and regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We can take that document off the screen now. I believe that we are going have to go back into private session for but a moment. And if we could have P757 up on the screen. And also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We are in private session, I think. And -- or not. Okay. Mr. Guy-Smith, are you asking that we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe we have to go into private session again because I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And could we have 757, P757, on the screen. It would be -- I believe it's page 4 in the B/C/S and page 3 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, you were asked by Mr. Thomas with regard to your report and specifically with regard to page 79 of your report, which is under paragraph 190, a number of questions concerning the 27th Session of the Supreme Defence Council held on the 27th of September, 1994. And I'd like to focus on --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I must say I don't recall asking those questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You know what, as a matter of fact, I stand corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I was wondering, myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I stand corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the SDC minutes and specifically with regard to the assertion that you've made concerning the 27th Session, you indicate: "The request to transfer the requested artillery ammunition to the Army of the Federal Republika Srpska is hereby refused since it is contrary to the decision by the federal government." If we could go -- which is a language which is also found in number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could go to the first page of this document so we can identify what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you identify for us what this document is that -- that has the language that I just read to you in number 6?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is the minutes of the 27th Session of the Supreme Defence Council, session held on the 27 of September, 1994. I see that the minutes were drawn up on the 1st of October, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we see number 6, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I was going to go back to it again. Can we now go back to page 4 in the B/C/S and page 3 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And looking at number 6 once again, what does that indicate?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 6 shows that the Supreme Defence Council did not accept the request of the Army of Republika Srpska to provide the requested ammunition because it was contrary to the decision of the federal government; that is to say that the federal government did not agree to give this kind of assistance to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if we could scroll down on the -- in the B/C/S to the bottom of the page so we can see whether or not that document was signed and by whom it was signed and in what capacity.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document was signed by Zoran Lilic, president of the Supreme Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could take that document off the screen, if we could go back into public session, and I will not be requesting to go back into private session again during the pendency of my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During your questioning earlier today by Mr. Thomas, you indicated, at page 67, line 3, you said: "In order to avoid any confusion, let me tell you this: This document is incorrect in a detail. Can I explain what is incorrect in it?" And then you went on to -- that request was denied to you, but I don't know whether or not you had an opportunity to continue your discussion with regard to P1214 as to the incorrect detail that you were referring to or not. And I couldn't -- I couldn't discern whether your answer that you ultimately made did include your ability to explain the incorrect detail that you had mentioned or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Don't you think that in fairness to the witness he should see P1214 on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, I do indeed. So if we could have that back up. And it's -- it's the -- and it's page 19 of both documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My question to you is: Did you get the opportunity when you were discussing this before to answer the question with regard to this -- I'm sorry. Did you get the opportunity to explain the incorrect detail that you were trying to establish with Mr. Thomas or not? And if you did not, what was it?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have an opportunity to explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Kindly do so now, sir.

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The explanation is as follows: You know that the Army of Republika Srpska used -- had its supplies from the reserves and from what was left when the JNA withdrew. In addition to that, they also purchased supplies from the territory of Federal Republic of Yugoslavia from the special-purpose industry. And they also received supplies through assistance of the VJ. When you see the column where it says received from the General Staff of Republika Srpska, you do not see anything that had been purchased from the special-purpose industry of Yugoslavia. And it is reasonable to assume that where it says GSV, that that represents the total amount of ammunition that had arrived from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, be it via purchase from special-purpose industry or through assistance received from the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And where are we supposed to see GSV? I'm asking you, Mr. Djokic. Where do we see GSV on this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's a column entitled, "received through the GS of the VRS," and then within that title, underneath, there is one sub-column: "From the government of the RS." That's one column. And then another column is "from the VJ." I apologise, it doesn't say "from the VS," it says "from the VJ." And then the third column is total. So the Army of Republika Srpska also purchased ammunition from the factories, and that data is missing in the column. And I think that in this column where it says "from the VJ" includes everything that had arrived from Yugoslavia; that is to say, what was received through assistance of the VJ and what was purchased in factories in the territory of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There has been some discussion with regard to documents that you --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, are you satisfied with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, I didn't get the answer to what GSV is, but I got the answer explaining what he -- [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Should we -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There's been -- there's been some discussion with regard to documents that you reviewed and some criticism that's been levied against you, and I just want to get one thing clear, which is with regard to the combat readiness report for the VJ for 1994, that was a document, was it not, that we requested from the National Council of Co-operation in --

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We don't have a question. Finish the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And we did not receive -- we requested the document from the National Council for the Co-Operation with The Hague for FRY, and we did not receive that document, did we?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to documents that you received from the Defence, we gave you the records of -- all of the trial records that we had, we gave that to you so you could use that in your analysis?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Earlier, in discussions in a question that was raised by Judge David, the issue of state secrets came up, and I'd like to just get kind of a rough, if I could, or general understanding of how the military -- the military operates. Now, the military operates on the basis of state secrets, does it not?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A certain number of decisions are classified as a state secret. That's normal in any army.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to the Supreme Defence Council sessions, to your knowledge those sessions in their entirety, until whatever revelation occurred here in The Hague, were also state secrets, were they not?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can give you the following answer: Before embarking upon working in this case, I did not have occasion to see any material from the Supreme Defence Council sessions except for the information which was published in the press, namely that such and such session of the Supreme Defence Council was held on such and such date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Djokic, I must implore you once again: Listen carefully to the question and answer the question and only the question. The question to you was: "... to your knowledge those sessions in the entirety, until whatever revelation occurred here in The Hague, were also state secrets, were they not?" Yes, they were; no, they were not; I don't know. One of those three. Then we go home quicker.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how they were classified.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In your research with regard to the issues that you were presented here, were you ever made aware of any super state secret documents above and beyond those state secret -- those documents that were comprised of the SDC sessions?

utterances.speaker: IVAN DJOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not come across a single document which received a higher classification than a state secret document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: One minute and I am probably done with my questioning. I do have two housekeeping matters. I have two housekeeping matters. Those housekeeping matters are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you done?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I am done with my questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we -- can we just wind up with the witness and then you can come to your housekeeping matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Oh, but of course. Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Djokic, thank you so much for taking the time off your very busy schedule to come and testify at the Tribunal. This brings us to the end of your testimony. You are now excused, you may go home. And please travel well back home. You may stand down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. We would tender those supporting materials that make up the footnotes with regard to Mr. Djokic's report in their entirety so that the Chamber has an opportunity to review those as well or refer to them, since they have come up during the course of this examination. I have been informed that they should all be -- which is why I was a bit -- I had some consternation, but they should all have been translated by CLSS and that full translations of all of those documents should have been delivered to the Office of the Prosecutor, and Mr. Thomas specifically. I had a bit of a concern when there was apparently some slippage there, but to the two issues; one is, I offer those apologies from the Defence to Mr. Thomas in that regard as well as to the Chamber because we were -- endeavoured madly to make sure that all of them were translated into English, and I know that there was a series of e-mails that when back and forth for probably some many weeks concerning that particular issue. And we'll make an appropriate designation of each of the footnoted documents for the purposes of the Chamber's edification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I hear what you say. And before I call on Mr. Thomas, just two remarks to make: First of all, that slippage you make, I can understand, but it should not have slipped to the extent that they were not footnoted; number one. Number two, it is not a housekeeping matter. Because if you want to tender them, this was the best witness to tender them through. Now you've let him go before tendering them. You are now virtually at the mercy of Mr. Thomas as to whether he's going to object or not object. Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand the mercy that I'm at.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And I'm feeling merciful, sir, so I have no objection to those documents being tendered. Perhaps in the instances where there is or has been a history of correspondence between the Defence and CLSS regarding translations, I wonder whether that continued. There were a couple of documents this morning which I undertook to arrange translations for, but given what my learned friend has said, it's probably best that the Defence be responsible for continuing those efforts they've already made and ensure that the translations are provided that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That would be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, fine. Thank you so much. Then I guess you'll tender them, and the Registrar can give them exhibit numbers outside court and tell us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Apparently the procedure is you've got to make a list of that and file it with the Registry and the Chamber will look at it and the Chamber will give instructions to the Registrar accordingly. So you may do that. Are you done with your housekeeping matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's -- I have two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the other is, is that during the testimony of Mr. Bildt on 27th of October, we presented him with two portions of previous testimony in this case without identifying the particular witness or the page numbers. We were informed by the Legal Officer that that would perhaps be appropriate. And we'd like to put on the record the portions of the transcript which we were citing at page 14278, at line 11, through 14279, line 2 of Mr. Bildt's testimony. We cited to the testimony of Muhamed Sacirbey taken on the 18th of June, 2009, transcript pages 2495 at line 23 through -- 7495 at line 23, through 7496, line 7. At page 14282, line 18, through 14283, line 24 of Mr. Bildt's testimony, we cited to the testimony of Muhamed Sacirbey taken on the 1st of July, 2009, transcript page 7736, lines 1 through 18. That concludes those matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Guy-Smith. The Chamber has its own housekeeping matters, just two also, very brief. Just two oral decisions that the Trial Chamber would like to render. On the 28th of September, 2010, the Defence filed a request for changing status of certain exhibits admitted under seal whereby it requests to change the status of certain exhibits originating from the disclosure batch 410 and relevant transcript portions. The Defence submits that following the Trial Chamber's decision of 12 August 2010 left in protective measures for disclosure batch 2410 material, the confidential status of the exhibits originating from batch 410 is no longer required. The Prosecution did not file a response to the Defence request. The Trial Chamber grants the request and directs the Registry to make public the exhibits and relevant transcript portions as identified in the Defence request. The second one. The Trial Chamber will now address some housekeeping matter here which is that on the 14th of October, 2010, the Defence filed a motion regarding marked-for-identification documents in which it notifies the Trial Chamber that it has received official CLSS translations of certain documents that were marked for identification pending official translation. The Defence now seeks leave to replace the draft translations in e-court with these official translations and have the document admitted into evidence. The Prosecution did not file a response to the Defence request. The Trial Chamber grants the motion, allows the Defence to replace the translations, directs the Registry to remove the MFI status of the exhibits listed in the motion and to take the necessary steps for the implementation of this decision. Thank you so much. Mr. Guy-Smith, to what date do we postpone?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The 15th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Apparently the lifting of that confidential status in the first decision, I guess, applies also to the audio-video recordings of those portions. Thank you so much. To what date shall we postpone, Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We request postponement to the 15th of November for our next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Does anybody know what time do we sit on the 15th, is it morning or afternoon? I see a finger says this court, but I don't see it saying what time. Okay. I guess it's going to be in the morning. Or whatever the time is, we will postpone to the 15th of November, time to be ascertained as time goes on. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: May I say one last thing which is thank you very much for accommodating me and having an extra session. I want to thank all of the staff and everybody who was involved in sitting later on a Friday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Guy-Smith. You're welcome. And I hope everybody has heard Mr. Guy-Smith's thanks. And I'm told the 15th is Monday morning. So it will be 9.00, Courtroom II. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
